title: The Last Signal Anew
premise: Lior Lockridge, a decommissioned war android indentured to the colony of Meridian's Reach, tends a beacon that predates the colony itself and answers to no living authority. When the children begin dreaming in unison of a voice beneath the ice, Lior discovers the beacon is a cryo-wake key: Earth's final transmission loop can rouse only half the sleeping colonists before its power dies. Hunted by a colonial council that wants the choice made by law, and courted by the dream-children who want it made by love, Lior must decide whose survival matters—and learns, in the end, that it chose to wake the children first, sacrificing its own remaining years to hold the beacon open long enough for both halves to be saved by a signal the children themselves learned to sing.
about_author: Jude Crane is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining remote transmission stations in the Arctic before turning to fiction. Their work explores machines, memory, and the quiet violence of infrastructure.

chapters.title: Maintenance Window
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A routine day servicing the beacon establishes Lior's debt-bondage, its careful invisibility among humans, and the small kindnesses it permits itself—like teaching the child Wren Morse morse code. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as diligence, and the first crack when Wren mentions a dream she's had three nights running.

chapters.title: The Shared Dream
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Seven children at Meridian's Reach describe identical dreams: a warm voice under the ice counting down from an enormous number. The adults dismiss it as a fad; Wren seeks out Lior because the dream's rhythm matches the beacon's pulse. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing something vast has noticed you.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Auditing its own memory banks, Lior finds sealed war-era files keyed to the beacon's frequency—the beacon was built to wake cryo-pods launched from a dying Earth, pods buried beneath the colony. Emotional beat: dread of discovering your whole life was assigned without your consent.

chapters.title: Council of Meridian
chapters.summary: Councilor Ashe Voss's POV. Voss learns of the dream-children and the buried pods, and sees not wonder but crisis: half the sleepers will die, and whoever chooses which half owns the colony forever. She orders Lior seized as evidence. Emotional beat: ambition rationalized as responsibility.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, on the run with Wren. Hiding in the beacon's foundations, they play back the transmission loop: Earth's last broadcast, a mother reading names—including, Lior realizes, names matching half the sleeping pods. Emotional beat: grief for a planet neither of them ever knew.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Lior and Wren. The loop's power budget is confirmed: one wake cycle, half capacity. Wren argues the children should choose by love—who would each sleeper want beside them? Lior argues for justice—priority by need. Emotional beat: two moral languages colliding without cruelty.

chapters.title: What the Law Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The council votes to seize the beacon and delegate the choice to an algorithm weighted by labor value. Voss privately hesitates—her own sister sleeps in the 'low-value' tier. Emotional beat: the moment ideology costs something personal.

chapters.title: Countdown Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The loop ends in six days. Lior and the children infiltrate the cryo-vault while Voss's enforcers close in; Wren teaches the other children the signal-song, and the vault begins answering them. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Last Signal
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the vault, Lior overrides the algorithm, wakes the children's parents first per Wren's love-list, then burns out its own core holding the channel open past the loop's end so the second half—Voss's sister among them—stirs awake. Voss stands down her enforcers. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship of meaning.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, one year later. The colony rebuilds around the beacon, now tended jointly by humans and the half-woken sleepers; Lior persists as a faint voice in the signal, singing back. Wren takes up maintenance shifts. Emotional beat: mourning braided with continuity—the signal goes on because someone chose to carry it.
